summary: The note describes how the Bruneian Empire gained opportunities to expand after the Majapahit empire declined following the death of its emperor, Hayam Wuruk. It also notes that Chinese Ming emperor Yongle, who took the throne in 1403, sent envoys to various countries inviting tribute, and that Brunei quickly joined the profitable tributary system with China.
one_line: Brunei's rise as an expanding power after Majapahit's decline and its entry into China's tributary system under the Ming emperor Yongle.
key_facts: After the death of its emperor, Hayam Wuruk, Majapahit entered a state of decline.
Majapahit was unable to control its overseas possessions after its decline.
The decline of Majapahit opened the opportunity for Bruneian kings to expand their influence.
Chinese Ming emperor Yongle ascended to the throne in 1403.
Yongle immediately dispatched envoys to various countries after ascending the throne.
The envoys invited various countries to pay tribute to the Chinese court.
Brunei immediately got involved in the lucrative tributary system with China.
The note describes the tributary system with China as lucrative.
